Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for providing oversight, enhanced continuity, expertise, and consultant capabilities for the Joint Manpower Division (JMD), Directorate for Manpower and Personnel for Joint Chiefs of Staff. The assignment also includes Joint Duty assignments with the Secretary of Defense, the Joint Staff, the Services, unified combatant commands, miscellaneous joint activities, and Defense Agencies.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: MISSION STATEMENT: The Joint Staff (JS) Manpower and Personnel Directorate provides manpower and personnel management policies, plans and oversight for all joint and combined activities reporting to or through the Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff. This includes the full range of joint manpower policy guidance and procedures for joint and international activities, providing manpower programming and resourcing support and developing joint plans, policies, and guidance concerning military and personnel readiness issues. Administers internal Joint Staff civilian and military personnel programs, including civilian senior executives; and developing a comprehensive human capital management strategy.
MajorDuties: As a SUPERVISORY MANAGEMENT ANALYST at the GS-0343-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Collaborate with the J1 and J8 Directorates to validate, document, defend, and develop resources to fund manpower requirements for the Joint Staff and Combatant Commands. Establish broadly defined objectives and goals for the branch with supervisory oversight. Perform and guide short and long-range planning, make work assignments and adjustments as necessary to accomplish the unit's mission. Monitor the status and progress of work and review completed work for sufficiency and administrative requirements. Serve as the Joint Staff expert on joint manpower resource issues. Develop, lead, and promote manpower policy and guidance for multi-Service manpower contributions through the Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff, to all Service components and joint activities. Develop, organize, and analyze assessments of joint manpower and prepare presentations and reports. Provide advice and participate in study groups which incorporate the areas of manpower. Formulate comprehensive decisions when evaluating and implementing joint manpower considerations in support of national and international policy. Develop options and recommendations for alternative manpower resourcing capabilities for decisions by Joint Staff senior leadership. Analyze and develop methods to determine the impact of functional alignment and changes or adjustments to current and proposed organizational structures in the joint community. Address and solicit for support for joint manpower requests. Assess each situation to ensure appropriateness and adequacy to the manpower request. Exercise independent and knowledge-based judgment to recommend changes or courses of action to achieve objectives and meet time-sensitive suspense's. Develop and lead manpower study proposals for all Combatant Commands, and report resources directly to the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Recommend modifications to joint manpower to the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and Secretary of Defense. Maintain comprehensive knowledge of worldwide political and military affairs. Manage all aspects of the manpower information systems Establish manpower requirements with Service databases and maintain Secretary of Defense program reporting requirements. Prepare proposals for manpower information systems; obtain funding, ensure system integration, information security, and modernization or system enhancements. Liaison with software analysts to more efficiently utilize current manpower data base systems. Enhance data comparability, ease of use, and applicability of manpower data. Provide guidance and advice on Programming, Planning, and Budgeting System (PPBS) to combatant commands, Combat Support Agencies, and Joint Staff concerning inclusion of applicable joint manpower in annual memorandums, submissions, and budget submissions. Analyze, develop input, and comment to Secretary of Defense ensuring joint manpower is properly addressed in a Resource Management Decision. Coordinate with Secretary of Defense on appropriate documentation for sourcing new and changing joint manpower requirements.

Applies knowledge of joint operations, joint doctrine and tactics, techniques and procedures to provide recommendations, guidance, and priorities to senior leaders on Global Force Management (GFM) programs. Plans and analyzes operational planning, global force management and strategy development for complex issues within integrated cross-functional teams and Combatant Commands (CCMDs). Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for leading the development of the Department's Force Management Framework and associated Directed Readiness Tables, as well as identifying and analyzing the required forces related to Force Assignment Tables
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-8 Directorate (Force Structure, Resources & Assessment) is charged with providing support to CJCS for evaluating and developing force structure requirements. J-8 conducts joint, bilateral, and multilateral war games and interagency politico-military seminars and simulations. It develops, maintains, and improves the models, techniques, and capabilities used by the Joint Staff and combatant commands to conduct studies and analyses for CJCS.
MajorDuties: As a STRATEGIC ANALYST OPS PLANNER at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Directs and manages the development and execution of all Global Force Management Implementation Guidance, Directed Readiness Tables, and Force Assignment Tables for the Secretary of Defense. Design, planning and productivity of a Department of Defense team comprised of force management experts from multiple Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Combatant Commands (CCMDs) and Department of Defense Components. Serves as principal and senior technical expert, analyst, and advisor to the senior most Joint Staff leadership on all joint force management matters related to DoD force assignment to Military Secretaries and CCMDs to include past and current Office of the Secretary of Defense Joint Staff (JS) policy decisions. Responsible for leading, and participating in, efforts spanning the planning, development, maintenance, production, and integration of Global Force Management strategic-level reform and initiatives that are aligned with the strategy and senior leader guidance. Assists Joint Staff lead for planning, organizing and executing CJCS Senior Seminar Series activities for the Department's senior-most leaders, intended to provide the Department's senior leadership with operational force management capability and capacity assessments through tabletop exercises designed to examine the Department's strategic force development policy and force planning issues. Responsible for gaining consensus where appropriate amongst the Department's senior most leadership, finding compromise positions and brokering agreeable decisions between Joint Staff offices, OSD staff & agencies, Combatant Commands and Service representatives.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This Acquisition Policy Specialist, NH-0301-03 position is located in the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Acquisition, Logistics and Technology) located at the Pentagon.
Details.SubAgencyName: Assistant Secretary of the Army (Acquisition, Logistics and Technology)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. The Army Acquisition Workforce is charged with a critical mission to cultivate innovation, design the impossible, and provide Soldiers with what they need to be successful. This is done through people-a workforce of more than 32,000 Army acquisition professionals from scientists and engineers to accountants and program managers who turn Army requirements into products and services, managing everything from cradle to grave. Civilians make up 96% of the Army Acquisition Workforce, and specialize in one of six functional areas and serve in over 20 commands stationed around the globe. For more information, visit: https://asc.army.mil/web/recruitment/
MajorDuties: Serves as the Army Acquisition Specialist, consultant and focal point for planning and developing policy initiatives for acquisition programs or issues with national and/or international scope and impact.
Provides authoritative advice to the Army Acquisition Executive (AAE) on program progress, new initiatives and efficiencies obtained from current initiatives.

Develops, plans, and interprets Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of the Army (DA) acquisition reform initiatives, Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition policy, and annual National Defense Authorization Acts (NDAAs).
Conducts strategic analysis regarding the relationships between statutory requirements, federal regulations, and DoD and Army policies to advise on policy development and acquisition reform efforts.
Collaborates with high-level teams working on complex acquisition-related endeavors.

If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. This is a DoD Demonstration Project position. Under the Defense Authorization Act, personnel management demonstration programs are operating in numerous Army activities and various other organizations supported by Army civilian personnel centers. Under the streamlined personnel operations for demonstration projects, the familiar 15 General Schedule grade structure is replaced with broad pay bands that typically encompass a range of grades. For example, acquisition jobs in level NH-03 of broad banding encompass the traditional GS-12 Step 1 through GS-13 Step 10 grades. Other initiatives under the demonstration projects include simplified classification, streamlined hiring process, and expanded developmental opportunities.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will lead studies, surveys, reviews, and/or research projects to evaluate program accomplishments, effectiveness, and/or compliance with meeting specific goals, objectives, rules, and regulations.

You will execute program plans to achieve milestones and requirements for the full scope of activities associated
with acquisition issues.
You will provide long range plans for the cost, performance, schedule of diverse teams and acquisition efforts within the scope of assigned areas

You will monitor and review performance by Government entities and contractors with respect to schedules, budget, resource utilization, and technical problems and initiates the appropriate corrective actions.
You will discuss developer issues and concerns, discuss and arbitrate courses of action, and oversee the COR (Contracting Officer Representative) duties to ensure full compliance.

You will provide authoritative input to budget plans and future FY funding needs, life cycle sustainment plans and activities, infrastructure upgrades and modifications, staffing plans, project timeline plans, and product enhancement opportunities.
You will plan and coordinate with requirements officers in planning for outyear projects.

You will participate in the development and presentation of numerous status reviews and high level oversight briefings by various customers to include resource sponsors, PMS340 management, and senior Navy staff.
You will ensures cost, schedule, performance, regulatory and statutory requirements, and customer expectations and requirements are balanced appropriately.
You will represent the program during leadership meetings, reviews, status briefings, and meetings with present and new customers from the Navy and other services.

You will collaborate on timelines for new project starts, ensures the acquisition team has sourced the necessary documentation to support project execution as planned, and help generate solutions for issues/concerns if necessary.

Details.RequiredDocuments:
You are required to provide documentation that supports the eligibility and qualification claims made in your resume and assessment questionnaire. You must submit the applicable documents listed here and those listed with the eligibilities you select in the announcement questionnaire with your application package. Applicants who do not provide supporting documentation that fully support their claims will not be referred to the hiring manager. Cover letter is optional. A complete resume is required. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume, but it is acceptable to provide elsewhere in your application package: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week, and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience.TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you applying for a promotion? To be considered for a promotion, you must provide SF-50(s) that shows that you have held the next lower GS grade for at least one year. SF-50s that have an effective date within the past year (e.g., General Adjustment SF-50 from this year or Within Rate/Grade Increases (WRI/WGI) SF-50 within a year) do not clearly show that you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement. That means if you submit an SF-50 that is dated within the last year, you must submit another SF-50 that is dated more than one year ago to clearly demonstrate you meet the time-in-grade requirements. If you are a DoD employee, you can obtain a copy of your SF- 50(s) from MyBiz. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume or assessment questionnaire regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference?
If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents contain personal information such as SSN and DOB and some documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove said personal information before you submit your application. You must provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName: Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-14 grade level, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Performing analysis and conducing special projects in Joint Logistics Operations, DoD Petroleum Supply Chain, Command and Control, Military Posture Plans, Theater Distribution Plans, and Global commercial and military Fuel Distribution. Managing, analyzing, and providing recommendations regarding multiple studies including identifying and analyzing the global petroleum supply chain as required by the Department of Defense's (DoD's) analytic agenda. Planning, conducting, coordinating, and evaluating complex planning products to conduct studies, technical analyses, synthesize/analyze complex issues, and present clear and concise technical recommendations to Joint Staff and analytic agenda leadership. Directing, leading, and managing major analytic studies and projects involving the application of a wide range of qualitative and quantitative methods sufficient to review, plan, execute and oversee administrative and technical work that is highly technical and difficult, e.g., involving petroleum, analytic agenda. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Will be responsible for Joint Policy advice, development, maintenance, and support, to inform senior decision makers regarding global petroleum matters. Will afford joint logistics enterprise command and control governance through representation and collaboration with the Office of Secretary of Defense (OSD), Combatant Commands (CCMDs), Military Departments, and the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-4 (Logistics,) leads the logistics enterprise, drive joint force readiness and provide the best logistics advice to the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, to maximize the joint force commander's freedom of action.
MajorDuties: As a SENIOR STRATEGIC ANALYST (PETROLEUM) at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Actively assesses the impact of policies and legislation on the integration efforts across the global U.S. Department of Defense petroleum supply chain. Analyzes and evaluates legislative proposals for potential impact on DoD petroleum supply and distribution programs. Analyzes management issues and problems, and resolves matters with relevant leadership members and senior subject matter experts. Manages and validates Joint Staff Bulk Petroleum Contingency Reports (REPOL), Bulk Petroleum Capabilities Report (POLCAP), Petroleum War Reserve Requirement (PWRR), Pre­Positioned War Reserve Stock (PWRS), Days of Supply (DOS) Guidance, the Inventory Management Plan (IMP), and various Situation Reports (SITREPs). Serves as the Combatant Commander's advocate in petroleum policy and doctrinal matters with a thorough understanding of and sensitivity to the needs of the joint force. Evaluates alternative strategies for solving daily analytic issues to fmd both technical and non-technical, cost-effective solutions
Details.Education: Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM ANALYST in the MILITARY PERSONNEL AND ANALYSES DIRECTORATE of ASSTSECNAV M-RA WASHINGTON DC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will develop and interpret military personnel policy, analyze strategy and policy recommendations, develop goals and milestones for the accomplishment of new initiatives, and monitor and oversee assigned policies and programs.

You will respond to inquiries and prepare products to Congress, field activities, special interest groups, and federal, state and local agencies on policy formulation and interpretation, program statistical data, status updates and funding issues.

You will analyze and evaluate policy, programs and budget for the Secretariat, provide advice to senior leadership on manpower and personnel policies and objectives, and ensure the effective and efficient implementation of personnel programs.

You will provide technical and analytical advice and support in portfolio responsibilities, manage the research and analysis portfolio, and implement studies to inform short and long-term military manpower and personnel policies and objectives.

You will design and execute research and analyses, build and use models to address issues/problem areas in military personnel policy, and plan, organize and lead others in carrying out complex research activities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities.Current Department of Army Civilian EmployeesInteragency Career Transition Assistance PlanLand Management Workforce Flexibility ActMilitary Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) EligibleVeterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998
In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes developing and recommending material requirements; overseeing fielding plans and force modernization activities; assisting with the development of the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) and Extended Planning Period (EPP) material/monetary requirements for assigned systems; converting senior leader guidance into program and budget instructions for systems. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas:
Oral CommunicationOrganizational Performance AnalysisRequirements Analysis
Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as Synchronization Staff Officer (SSO), Action Officer (AO), and principal representative for G-8, Force Development Directorate in matters pertaining to one or more assigned systems. Manages those assigned systems to ensure manpower, money, and material resources are properly allocated to support timely development, procurement, and fielding of new items and appropriate cascading of replaced items.
Details.SubAgencyName: Deputy Chief of Staff G-8, Force Development, Directorate of Materiel
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Assist with developing strategy and justification of resources to support system requirements to Army leadership, Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and Congress, resulting in funding of programs.
Coordinate with leadership to obtain program support and to ensure program success.
Assist with new acquisition strategies to meet established priorities for assigned systems.
Coordinate with Organizational Integrators to ensure force structure and hardware fielding is compatible.
Analyze and identify potential for joint programs with other Services and allied nations and make recommendations for programs.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for directing and overseeing the development, implementation, assessment, and refinement of strategies, plans, and policies to support the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (CJCS) to fulfill his global military integration function.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-5 (Strategic Plans and Policy) proposes strategies, plans, and policy recommendations to the CJCS to support his provision of "military advice" across the full spectrum of national security concerns to the President and other national leaders and to ensure those recommendations are informed by a larger strategic context coordinated with interagency and alliance partners, account for the view and requirements of the combatant commanders, and assess risk in executing the National Military Strategy.
MajorDuties: As a STRATEGIC PLANNER at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: This position represents the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (CJCS) for all matters relating to strategies, plans and policies in support of the CJCS statutory global military integration function. This position is required to regularly interact with General Officer/Flag Officer and Senior Executive Service members within DoD, various US Government Departments and Agencies (such as the Departments of State, Homeland Security, Treasury and the National Counterterrorism Center), as well as with key U.S. Ally and Partner nations. Uses analytical judgment to review, and initiates changes to military strategies, policies and procedures to ensure that the Joint Force has sufficient capacity and capability to achieve National Defense Strategy (NDS), and National Military Strategy (NMS) objectives. Conduct research, compose and present position papers, and manage and lead supporting projects and programs to completion.
Details.Education: Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Program Analyst within the Joint Service Provider (JSP), Business Resource Center, Acquisition Division, supporting the agency?s Information Technology acquisition program.
Engage in program-related data collection and analysis; assisting JSP requirement owners and stakeholders in defining, documenting, planning, and execution of requirements.
Participate in the development of acquisition strategy and development of acquisition packages.

Liaise with contracting organizations regarding the completion and award of service contracts, post award Contracting Officer?s Representative services, including contract compliance management, performance evaluation, and contract closeout support.

Provide an essential service by integrating technical aspects with program management and contractual matters, including planning and scheduling, budgeting, expenditure accounting, and program analysis reporting.
Perform continuing analyses of the effectiveness, efficiency, cost effectiveness, schedule adherence, and other key parameters of the acquisition program?s progress and success.
Assist in the development, documentation, and improvement of business processes, procedures and best practices. Based on analytical results and reports, identify potential problem areas.

Prepare and coordinate program budget requests, justifications, and other financial planning documents that are fully defensible and adhere to governing Army, DoD, and Federal Directives, policies and regulations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: COVID-19 Vaccination: To ensure compliance with an applicable preliminary nationwide injunction, which may be supplemented, modified, or vacated, depending on the course of ongoing litigation, the Federal Government will take no action to implement or enforce the COVID-19 vaccination requirement pursuant to Executive Order 14043 on Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees. Therefore, to the extent a Federal job announcement includes the requirement that applicants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 pursuant to E.O. 14043, that requirement does not currently apply. Federal agencies may request information regarding the vaccination status of selected applicants for the purposes of implementing other workplace safety protocols, such as protocols related to masking, physical distancing, testing, travel, and quarantine. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the NH-04 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-3 (or GS-13) grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability researching, analyzing, and synthesizing conflicting information and data to formulate policies and procedures governing congressional affairs; and to respond to legislative inquiries. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD (R&E)). The USD(R&E) serves as the Chief Technology Officer and is responsible for research, development, and prototyping activities within the Department of Defense (DoD).
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research & Engineering (USD(R&E))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Chief Technology Officer and is responsible for research, development, and prototyping activities within the Department of Defense (DoD); Facilitates open lines of communication and understanding, maintaining and/or establishing close working relationships with the OUSD (R&E) Front Office, Deputy Chief Technology Officers (DCTO) and Principal Directors, Directors, USD(R&E) Staff Principals, ASD Legislative Affairs (OSD(LA)), USD Comptroller Budget Affairs and Activity (BAA) Office, JCS Legislative Liaison, and legislative liaison offices of military Services; Works with OSD(LA) and BAA to maintain and update appropriate biographical information on all Members of the House or Senate and key congressional staff, including the Members most current research and engineering interests and concerns; Ensures all House or Senate activities (trips, meetings, and hearings) are communicated to OUSD(R&E) and senior leaders in a timely manner; Ensures Senior OUSD(R&E) leaders are aware of key decision points so that they can affect the process at the right time and place; Provides assistance at hearings of congressional committees and bodies, analyzes discussions from these meetings and outlines the concerns and issues that may require incorporation into the OUSD and DCTO's congressional communication engagement strategy.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located within the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), which falls under the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)). Its mission OFR is to strengthen and promote the resiliency and readiness of the Total Force by developing integrated policies, oversight, and synchronization of activities in the areas of diversity management, personnel risk reduction, suicide/sexual assault prevention, and collaborative efforts with the Dept. of Veterans Affairs.

OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Supports integrated prevention programs and associated program requirements and objectives, such as Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, the Military Departments and Services, OUSD (P&R), Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), VA, interagency meetings, and topic-specific groups covering integrated prevention, and/or issues relevant to the missions and objectives of OFR. Develops strategic, programmatic, and policy recommendations, and provides evidence-based rationale for integrated prevention program recommendations. Develops, coordinates, and finalizes recommendations for policy inputs impacting DoD and Military Department and Service regulatory guidance. Develops, reviews, and provides feedback and coordination on briefs, information papers, and other strategic communication materials. Reviews, analyzes, and edits annual and special reports OFR submits to various entities and ensures they articulate all reporting requirements; supports OFR's congressional/legislative work including staffing, research, analysis, and formulation of official responses to from Members of Congress, their staffs, and congressional committees. Monitors the Defense Appropriation and Authorization Bill processes, including subcommittee and committee hearings, deliberations on the House and Senate floors, and passage into Public Law.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-14, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes managerial experience that will enable the employee to provide technical and managerial expert advice for operating all programs assigned, which impact the Pentagon, other NCR facilities occupied by HAF personnel, and Site R. Knowledge on setting uniform standards for facilities that will support grade structures and positions that run from the lowest enlisted grades through 4-star generals/civilian equivalents and that support security classification levels from unclassified to as high as Top Secret/SCI/SAP. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of operations, products, services, need, and goals of this program(s) and the organizations studied or served, and related customers, functions, resources, and users. Knowledge of standard contracting regulations, practices, and procedures. Knowledge of automated data processing concepts, systems capabilities, and economic usage to effectively complete assignments. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Knowledge of work classifications and the regulatory and statutory restrictions on the expenditures of appropriated and non-appropriated funds. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of an organization through subordinate supervisors. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of one or more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Ability to communicate both orally and in writing. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

The selectee's salary will be set within the grade equivalent to a GS/GG grade based on the selectee's qualifications in relation to the job. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: Having the quality level experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. My experience includes a background of education, training, and progressively more responsible professional experiences in government or business organizations responsible for complex programs of national significance based on work with/or in the Intelligence Community (IC). Knowledge of IC contract negotiation, administration, and termination principles, policies, procedures, and technical requirements applicable to pre-award and post-award actions for a variety of contracts; of business practices and market conditions applicable to program and technical acquisition requirements; and of price and cost analysis sufficient to review proposals against previous history, actual and estimated expenditures, and established rates to determine price reasonableness or to determine a negotiation position. Must have broad-based experience at the expert level to perform the full range of analytical functions for understanding Competitive Sourcing and Privatization (CS&P) contracting processes and procedures. The work requires knowledge of a wide range of concepts, principles, and practices in a professional or administrative occupation, such as would be gained through extended graduate study or experience and skill in applying this knowledge to difficult and complex work assignments. Note: Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector, or experience gained in another government agency. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Expert knowledge of the full range of federal contracting laws, regulations, policies, practices, methods, and contract types 2. Expert knowledge of qualitative and quantitative analytical methods and the ability to apply this knowledge to complex problems of broad scope. 3. Comprehensive knowledge and understanding of J-32/JISROC CCA missions, goals, and objectives, business and strategic plans, etc. 4. Expert / demonstrated skill in communicating, both orally and in writing; writing clear and concise products; presenting and argueing for a position effectively; and delivering written and verbal presentations to senior level audiences for decision-making purposes. 5. Expert knowledge and experience coordinating joint actions across CCMD, Military Service, Joint Staff Directorate, and Office of Secretary of Defense staffs to perform varied tasks associated with coordinating input, tracking status, reporting on issues, and developing recommendations/solutions to assist senior decision-making. 6. Demonstrated ability to conduct detailed analysis of contracting requirements to develop feasible courses of action and identify optimal sourcing recommendations. Ability to analyze all aspsects of a complex and contentious issue; think creatively to develop and implement new methods, approaches, processes and/or procedures to effectively address problems. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: Analyzing
effectiveness of current operations and proposes strategies for productivity enhancements, optimal organization structures, and effective resource allocation for JIOWC operational plans and objectives; Establishes and maintains relationships by liaising with key organizations; and Advising and proves counsel to employees regarding policies, procedures, and directives of management. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Expert knowledge of Information Operations, intelligence, and military operations and Mastery knowledge of CCMD operations and agency disciplines to identify specific issues requiring trans-regional, multi-agency, and multi-disciplinary solutions. Mastery knowledge of the Joint Planning and Execution Community, the Joint Operation Planning Process, and resource planning. Knowledge of all Joint Information Operations functional disciplines and intimate knowledge of current JOWC responsibilities/capabilities, and the relationship with JS, OSD, CCMDs, and other agencies. Knowledge of management principle, processes, and analytical techniques for assessing programs; expertise in developing strategies for operational improvements and efficiencies. Skill in establishing and maintaining effective relationships, building consensus and coalitions, negotiating, and resolving conflict. Skill in oral and written communication and experience delivering information to senior leaders. Ability to effectively organize and analyze information; produce reports, position papers, and briefings that meet the specific needs of senior management officials/senior leaders; present clear and concise findings; resolve conflicts based on mature judgement, experience, and recognized professional standing; and effectively advocate for a position. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of an organization through subordinate supervisors. OTHER SIGNIFICANT FACTS: Position is designated special-sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position. A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. Drug Testing: This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. Key: The duties of this position meets all requirements as a category 4 designation, and shall not be vacated during a national emergency or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency or office to function effectively. This position must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CAN NOT become a member of the Ready Reserve. (IAW: DoDD 1200.7, "Screening the Ready Reserve,") Mobility: Mobility is a condition of employment. The employee must sign an Air Force-wide mobility agreement. (Note: See AFI36-202, dated 19 Aug 2019 for guidance) Polygraph: Incumbent is required to undergo a counterintelligence-scope polygraph examination. The employee may be required to travel in military and/or commercial aircraft to perform temporary duty assignments. The employee may be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and/or holidays. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS) position implemented under Section 504, Title V of Public Law 99-569, Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1987, as codified in Sec 1601, Chap 83 of Title 10 United States Code which sets forth Air Force policies and procedures for DCIPS. This position is in the Excepted Service. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. For additional information on DCIPS, click here
MajorDuties: As Director of Operations, manages and oversees functions responsible for the analysis, evaluation, and implementation of effective programs in JIOWC operations, intelligence, and OPSEC areas. Analyzes effectiveness of current operations and proposes strategies for productivity enhancements, optimal organization structures, and effective resource allocation for JIOWC operational plans and objectives. Conducts mission-related coordination and builds coalitions with NCR- and CCMD-based organizations and leads integration of the Information Joint Function in plans across OSD, JS, and other organizations. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Selects or recommends selection of candidates for vacancies, promotions, details, and reassignments in consideration of skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO and diversity objectives. Implements approved operations policies, directives and plans. Analyzes and interprets applicable regulations, directives, and documents and ensures that organizational directives and policy instruments are consistent with these directives.

Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service which includes applying education, prevention and response efforts in relation to harmful behaviors such as sexual assault/harassment, domestic violence, and substance abuse; developing and/or recommending solutions to reduce harmful behaviors; collaborating with stakeholders (DoD counterparts, Academia, Industry leaders) to solve complex problems; preparing and presenting a variety of evidence based prevention solutions for leaders to make executive level decisions; developing annual Army budget requirements for primary prevention activities. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service (GS-14 or equivalent). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas:
AccountabilityCost-Benefit AnalysisInfluencing/NegotiatingOral Communication

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as a Senior Advisor For Harmful Behavior Prevention Policy for the Office of the Secretary of the Army (Manpower & Reserve Affairs), located at the Pentagon in Arlington, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Provide professional guidance, advice, and decision support to Senior Army leadership on all matters pertaining to primary prevention.
Assist managers with financial expenditures and budgets associated with programing, planning, budgeting and execution (PPBE) of primary prevention.
Collaborate with Prevention Program Managers and Commands to incorporate and achieve Army prevention goals and objectives.
Perform oversight of the development and execution of guidance and policy related to all areas of prevention of harmful behaviors
Coordinate the development of prevention policy with appropriate agencies as the ASA (Manpower and Reserve Affairs) representative for the prevention of harmful behaviors
Prepare and oversee preparation of executive correspondence, presentation materials, briefings, assessments and proposals.
Maintain effective oversight of the Armys Primary Prevention System that encompasses human resources, collaborative relationships and infrastructure.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as a senior program analyst, participates and provides expertise in all aspects of the Army Planning, Programming, and Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) with special emphasis on the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) for continuity and effective management of assigned MM PEG programs. Works under the administrative direction of the Deputy, Resources Division who responds to the Chief, Resources Division, Director, Plans and Resources, Deputy Chief of Staff, G-1.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Manipulate and analyze data with complex structure using spreadsheets (excel pivot tables) and analytic software packages (such as tableau, minitab, sas, etc.).
Access and query data in data warehoused.
Load data and generate reports through defined user interface and business intelligence tools.
Research historic files and audit transaction history to provide forensic analysis of fiscal transactions.
Provide Army Senior Leaders and Commanders with simple, easily understandable narratives that they can articulate.
Perform detailed analysis, to include modeling and forecasting, in a high stakes, time constrained environment.

Utilize knowledge of the Federal Budget process, congressional committee structure as it relates to the Department of Defense (DoD) PPBE process, legislative process dealing with defense authorization and appropriations.

ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Conducts evaluations of programs and operational processes involving special operations Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) forces using a variety of qualitative and quantitative methods to provide advice and recommendations to superiors to improve efficiency and effectiveness throughout the organization. Develops, coordinates, manages, and represents DoD policies and programs related to Service-Secretary-like oversight of USSOCOM's special operations C4I forces. Participates and assists in the presentation of OSD policies and budgets to DoD, Congress, other USG agencies, and the general public. Plays a major role in the study, review, evaluation and adjustment of the strategies, concepts, special operations C4I programs, and budgets required to support OSD policy and program planning guidance

The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications, education, and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary:
The DCIO (SAP IT) is a direct report to the DoD CIO that leads, directs, and manages a staff comprised of senior executive service
(SES), civilian, military, and contractor personnel, providing expert management and oversight of the SAP IT enterprise, including
capabilities, architecture, requirements, cybersecurity, policy, governance, oversight and business operations to satisfy warfighter
SAP needs.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Department of Defense Chief Information Officer
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Responsible for the programmatic aspects of resource management in the annual planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) cycle as it relates to the areas under the DCIO SAP IT purview and across the DoD SAP community. Developing, implementing, and continuously improving DCIO SAP IT processes, methods, technology, and techniques to conduct requirements validation and PPBE activities. Analyzing, evaluating, coordinating, and integrating DCIO SAP IT's activities and deliverables related to the annual POM review. Leading resource management team and assessing progress of assigned projects or programs and keeping records of schedules, cost estimates and expenditures, monitoring contractor's acquisition development up to production and deployment, planning and coordinating activities of data and resource management and other activities, taking actions to approve contracts, budgets, terms and other conditions related to the contractor, and ensuring maintenance of documentation. Reviewing and providing short notice, quick-reaction analyses of critical programmatic issues and providing data to assist in preparation for legislative hearings, program documentation, briefing packages and read-aheads, Congressional staffer visits, and other events to ensure an integrated and consistent position across DCIO SAP IT and DoD CIO, and the Military Services and DAFAs SAP IT equities, in response to Congressional questions, issues, and requests for information on assigned program/portfolio.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. Qualifying Experience:
To qualify at the GG-12 level, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level (GG-11) in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: assisting in the development of administrative policies and procedures relating to management systems and responding to administrative inquiries. To qualify at the GG-13 level, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level (GG-12) in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: developing administrative policies and procedures relating to management systems, monitoring action or suspense items for timeliness and completion, and responding to and resolving complex administrative inquiries. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is being recruited under 10 USC 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It has been identified as a position necessary to carry out and support the mission of the US Cyber Command. It is in the Professional Work Category at the Full Performance Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. It is located in the DISA-Joint Service Provider (JPA2).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Develop policies and procedures regarding the administrative work processes and operations. Write, establish, and implement administrative policies and procedures to ensure effective management systems.

Execute the internal management control program for Joint Service Provider (JSP). Function as a communications expert for the organization. Undertake studies and projects that result in significant communication improvements for JSP.

Ensure the coordination, adequacy, and timeliness of all suspense items from the Command Group on staff and Center actions and other various issues. Determine action required for each suspense item and assign to appropriate office.

Keep the Chief and required parties advised of controversial and time-sensitive issues. Maintain a list of current action items and their status. Provide advice and assistance to management concerning office functions and missions.

Serves as the lead project officer for the development and the on-going upgrade of Directorate-wide workflow processes. Analyze the accuracy and validity of the products and provide recommended changes and improvements on an on-going basis

Engage in oversights of a variety of analytical studies and office/administrative services. These services include, travel, training, space management, timekeeping, brief preparation, correspondence preparation and review.

Assign work based on priorities, consideration of the difficultly and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees. Review, accept and reject work products. Give advice to employees on work and administrative matters.
Details.Education: There is no substitution of education for the qualifying experience at the GG-13 grade level
